evidence.observation: The candidate-bound report retains an immediate, direct presentation of Jamie as a Technical Project Manager focused on Product Operations and Implementation, with work, resume, and contact paths.
The role-fit surface continues to connect requirements, workflows, documentation, coordination, implementation, and durable handoffs to named public-facing projects.

The added early-organizer claim stays within contemporaneous reporting: it identifies Jamie as an organizer working with artists and venue communities while explicitly declining sole-leadership, sole-founding, or ownership claims.
The mutual-aid count remains correctly attributed as something Jamie said. The canonical boundary states that the source is not an independent audit of signups or active participation.

The October 2017 town-hall claim assigns the organizing action to NYC Artist Coalition and identifies Jamie only among coalition participants. It avoids an attendance total, exact individual production responsibilities, and individual policy causality.

The 2018 testimony claim is limited to Jamie's documented appearance, coalition affiliation, affordability-and-safety argument, and support for the Small Business Jobs Survival Act; it does not imply bill authorship, passage, or sole campaign leadership.

The Talks Not Raids campaign claim describes the public interface and coalition materials without assigning Jamie individual authorship. The Local Law claim separates campaign support for Intro 1156 from the Council record showing nineteen sponsors and enactment as Local Law 220 of 2019, preserving the explicit no-causal-share boundary.

All added claims use canonical Claim projections with mapped public sources, support descriptions, non-support boundaries, and rendered citations. Candidate evidence reports thirteen references, thirteen backlinks, nine source notes, accessible labels, and working local citation navigation.

The new 'A wider operating record' section is scannable and uses concise canonical statements, but seven additional cited claims increase the density of an already long case study. Repeated collective-credit and private-boundary explanations keep it strong rather than exceptional.

Jamie is visible through organizer attribution, testimony, documentation architecture, translation, coordination, and direct web-infrastructure work. Coalition organization, campaign interfaces, legislative outcomes, and policy leadership retain collective or institution-specific credit.

The public page describes private notes, legal-review materials, strategy documents, stakeholder lists, emails, and unapproved quotations only as intentionally omitted categories. No protected locator, private path, raw record, stakeholder list, private correspondence, or legal-review content appears in the inspected public materials.

The portfolio still relies primarily on text and representative artifact descriptions rather than approved visual artifacts. This is unchanged from the prior judgment and is an expressly permitted application-ready deferral.

The expanded 2017-2019 operating record is consistent with the established 2017-present NYC Artist Coalition chronology and does not alter the later 2024-present Commercial Rent Stabilization collaboration boundary.

Canonical metadata, Open Graph title and image, Twitter card, resume download, and contact paths remain present under staging defaults; production sharing verification remains outside this profile.

The report is bound to the requested candidate and records route, responsive, keyboard, citation, metadata, and resume-download evidence. Production smoke, deployed-commit verification, indexing approval, monitoring, and rollback evidence remain outside application-ready scope.
